title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-ethan-carter
content:
Target account: Nexvia Health (clinical documentation SaaS)

Quick profile (open-source/notes):
- HQ: Boston, MA
- Size: ~450 employees, Series C (2024)
- Tech stack: primarily AWS (EKS), some GCP for analytics, Kafka, Postgres.
- Use case: clinical note summarization + billing code suggestion + physician search over EMR docs.
- Current approach: internal Nirvana-LLM wrapper + OpenAI for spike features (costs rising, inconsistent latency).
- Compliance: HIPAA + SOC2 in progress; active interest in private deployments/bring-your-own-key.
- Buying center: Head of Product (Maya Ortiz), CTO (Ravi Gupta), Director of ML Ops (Leo Park), Security (Anya Chen).

Why they might care (pain hooks):
- Cost shock: current OpenAI spend spiked Q4; team seeking unit-cost predictability.
- Latency: doctors need realtime-ish summarization in the EHR UI (prefer <300ms 95th).
- Data residency & compliance: want private/VPC option + KMS/HSM for keys.
- Model drift & quality monitoring: need evals and rollback/AB testing for model updates.

Value props to lead with:
- Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput & SLOs) -> solves latency + 95th% control.
- Private deployment option with KMS integration -> HIPAA-friendly, audit logs.
- Cost controls: batching/caching + quantization profiles = 3-5x token cost reductions vs naive OpenAI usage for repeated patterns.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency dashboards + per-route quality regressions -> lowers operational risk for ML team.

Discovery / qualification questions (for first call):
- Where are you currently hosting inference (cloud, regions)? Any constraints on data egress?
- What % of requests are interactive vs background? Typical sequence lengths?
- SLOs you care about (p50/p95 latency targets)?
- Current monthly inference spend and forecast?
- Any constraints on bringing keys or running within customer VPC / on-prem?
- Who owns procurement for infra (platform vs finance)?

Outbound email drafts (A/B test):
--- Draft A (short) ---
Subject: Cut inference cost + stabilize latency for Nexvia notes
Hi Maya — quick intro, Ethan at Redwood Inference. We help teams running clinical LLM features move from variable OpenAI bills to predictable, dedicated inference with HIPAA-friendly private deployments.
If you have 15 mins this week I can share a short analysis of possible cost/latency gains for Nexvia based on public signals.
Thanks,
Ethan

--- Draft B (longer, value-led) ---
Subject: 3 ways to reduce LLM unit-costs for clinical summarization
Hi Maya / Ravi — Ethan from Redwood Inference. Noticed Nexvia’s work on in-EHR summarization — nice stuff. A few quick notes from similar customers: 
1) Dedicated GPU pools reduce tail latency variability (helps keep p95 <300ms)
2) Prefix/KV caching cuts tokens for repeated patient templates by ~30-50%
3) Private deployments + KMS meet audit requirements and remove data egress concerns
If you’re open, I can 1) send a short cost model with conservative numbers, and 2) walk through architecture compatibility (EKS + VPC).
Would next Tue/Thu 20-30min work?

Call script (15 min intro):
- 0:00-1:00 Quick intro + one-sentence value prop
- 1:00-4:00 Ask discovery questions (see above); try to get current infra + spend numbers
- 4:00-8:00 Walk through 1-2 specific ways Redwood would plug into their stack (Dedicated vs Private). Keep it concrete: where the model runs, how keys handled, sample latency numbers.
- 8:00-12:00 Objections & technical deep dives (if engineer on call).
- 12:00-15:00 Next steps (trial, pilot scope, exec alignment).

Objection handling cheatsheet (short):
- "We're using OpenAI and it works" -> Great — many customers start there. If your main issues are cost/latency/compliance we can sit on top of compatible model APIs or provide dedicated/private options that give SLA and cost predictability. We can run a side-by-side for 2 weeks.
- "We can't move PHI outside" -> We offer Private deployment (VPC + on-prem options) and KMS/HSM integration for key control. We can sign BAAs and provide audit logs.
- "We don't want to manage infra" -> Redwood Dedicated is fully managed GPU pools with autoscaling and SLA; we handle runtime and orchestration. Private deployments have a lighter control plane option if you prefer less ops overhead.
- "Quality/regressions are risky" -> Our console includes evals and promptset-based regression alerts; we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model variants.

Quick ROI sketch (back-of-envelope):
- Current: 200k tokens/day via OpenAI (avg cost $0.02/token -> $4k/day).
- With Redwood batching/caching + quantization: estimated 3x token efficiency -> $1.3k/day. Dedicated discount + commit -> further 20% reduction.
- Pilot ask: 30-day pilot on dedicated capacity for one model w/ basic observability -> target 30%+ cost reduction and p95 <300ms.

Notes for pilot proposal:
- Scope: clinical summarization endpoint (one route), 30D, prod-like traffic (peak hours simulated), logging/audit retention 90d, KMS integration.
- Success metrics: cost per completed summary, p95 latency, no PII leakage in logs, model output quality (BLEU/ROUGE proxies + small human eval).
- Risks: labeled eval set availability (we may need 200-500 prompts + labels), infra networking constraints (eg egress blocked).

To-dos / next steps (my side):
- [ ] Build quick cost model for Nexvia from public usage signals (ETA 2 days)
- [ ] Draft pilot proposal + SOW template (collab with Priya)
- [ ] Align with solutions-engineering for feasibility check (ticket SALES-482)
- [ ] Prep demo data (anonymized sample prompts) request to Maya if intro connects

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep emails short for Maya (product leader). Ravi (CTO) will want numbers and architecture. Leo (ML Ops) will nit latency and model checkpoint/quantization strategy. Anya (security) cares about keys/KMS and audit trails.
- Possible internal champion: Leo Park (likes quantization talk). Try to get 1:1 with Leo during discovery.
- If procurement is slow, propose 8-12 week proof-of-value instead of annual commit.

Slack snippets to use during intro thread:
"Ethan Carter from Redwood — we help teams running clinical LLM features stabilize latency & cut inference costs while meeting HIPAA controls. Short call to share a tailored cost model?
"
